item.title: New study demonstrates the impacts of multiple stressors on reef-building corals
item.description: New research shows Staghorn Coral may prove resilient to a single environmental stressor, but prove less resilient when facing a combination of stressors simultaneously.

item.title: Five ways NOAA research is making your life better—right now
item.description: Benefits include improved wildfire forecasts, safer drinking water, better flood predictions, sea floor mapping, and healthier fisheries.

item.title: Injecting light-reflecting particles into the stratosphere could also make marine clouds brighter
item.description: New research finds that diffusion of sunlight from particles in Earth’s stratosphere could indirectly make marine clouds thousands of feet below more reflective.

item.title: Global analysis reveals wildland-urban interface fires carry higher health burden
item.description: Although wildland-urban interface fires make up a small fraction of total fire emissions, they are responsible for a much larger share of smoke-related premature deaths.

item.title: New article on humid heat trends in the Southeast United States
item.description: Humid heat often worsens health risks of extreme heat by compromising human cooling mechanisms (sweating).

item.title: Confronting climate models with observations: a global assessment of simulated and historical climate trends
item.description: A new study finds that while climate models have successfully captured many global warming trends, such as rising temperatures and more intense downpours, they still fall short in key areas.

item.title: New research offers insights into why climate models often get spring El Niño forecasts wrong
item.description: Climate model overconfidence when predicting El Niño from March through May might result from models leaning too heavily on tropical Pacific signals.

item.title: Cooking emissions rival fossil fuels as an ozone pollution source in Los Angeles
item.description: As the adoption of cleaner-burning engines and electric vehicles drives fossil fuel emissions lower, volatile organic compounds from cooking are playing a significant role in ozone over Los Angeles.

item.title: Bringing storm surge to virtual reality
item.description: A new virtual reality simulation will use the idea that “seeing is believing” to show people why coastal evacuation orders are so important during storms.

item.title: Scientists at AOML monitor the impacts of ocean acidification on reefs with new series of buoys
